text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key practice is following naming conventions. This means choosing clear and meaningful names for variables, so others can quickly see what they represent. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on one task. When a function does too many things, it becomes hard to follow and test. Clean code also supports maintainability. If your code is well organised, it is much easier to find and fix bugs later. In short, writing clean code saves time and helps teams work together more effectively.
